clusters.state_of_play: Israeli settlers are escalating a campaign of violence and land expansion across the West Bank: besieging Palestinian homes in villages like Qusra (cutting off food and water), setting fire to a Palestinian home while a mother and her children slept inside, and resettling evacuated sites like Kadim two decades later. On Friday, Israeli settlers and soldiers killed two Palestinians in separate West Bank incidents: 17-year-old Karim Sanad Shalaldeh, shot by settlers, and 58-year-old Fathi Khazem, killed by Israeli forces. Video also emerged of Israeli soldiers themselves throwing belongings out of a besieged Palestinian home in Qusra, alongside settler sieges. Palestinian American homeowner Louai (Loui) Abo Ridi, back from Ohio after 10 days under siege, has directly confronted settlers outside his home despite Israeli military deployment, demanding protection from Israeli forces and the U.S. government. A new Yesh Din report finds settler attacks in Palestinian-administered West Bank areas have almost doubled since 2025 amid a self-proclaimed 'great settlement revolution,' with AJLabs analysis putting the rate at six attacks a day. Separately, settler children attacked a Red Crescent ambulance, the Board of Peace reversed course on a Gaza disarmament deal, Christian families report growing pressure to leave, and Israel opened tenders for over 1,200 homes in the E1 settlement, prompting France, Germany, Britain and Italy to join Europe and Canada in condemning the plan as making Palestinian statehood impossible. An Israeli minister also faces backlash over a gallows site with a 'viewing booth' for hanging Palestinians.
